haiku-low.q1: Neither response differs in status or message: both get HTTP 401 and show "Invalid email or password". Timing may differ, since unknown emails skip the bcrypt check; the document leaves that open.
haiku-low.q2: It is refused with HTTP 429 for 15 minutes. The password is not checked, the attempt is not recorded as a failure, and the lock is not extended.
haiku-low.q3: The existing session is deleted. The new session is created and the old one deleted in one database transaction, after the cookie's session ID is read.
haiku-low.q4: Only a random session ID, nothing else. It is in the sid cookie, flagged HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: At 12 hours after login, even with constant use. The 30-minute idle timeout resets on each request, but expires_at is fixed at login plus 12 hours.
haiku-low.q6: It clears the sid cookie and redirects to /login. The session check runs one query, and an unknown or expired session is treated as no session.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session named by the cookie, if any, before replying. Then it clears the cookie and redirects to /login. If the session is already gone, the reply is the same.
haiku-low.q8: In the Postgres sessions table. Each request looks up the session ID there, so either app instance can answer it. No sticky sessions are used.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failed attempt with email and failed_at. The document says only that five failures within any 10-minute period trigger a lock; it does not specify how the window is computed.
haiku-low.q10: It checks that the session exists, expires_at is in the future, and last_seen_at is within the last 30 minutes. When valid, it sets last_seen_at to now.
haiku-low.q11: HTTP 503 with "Sign-in is unavailable right now. Try again shortly." No cookie is set, the transaction is rolled back, and the old session stays.
haiku-low.q12: The cleanup job, which runs on a timer and deletes sessions past expires_at or idle over 30 minutes. The run interval is not yet chosen.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ: both get HTTP 401 and the login page showing "Invalid email or password". (Only possible difference is timing, which is an open question.)
sonnet.q2: The email is locked (lock set at the 5th failure), so the login is refused with HTTP 429 and a lockout message on the login page. The password is not checked, the attempt is not recorded as a failure, and the lock is not extended. The lock lasts 15 minutes.
sonnet.q3: The old session (the one the incoming cookie pointed to) is deleted, and a new session with a new random ID is created, both in one database transaction.
sonnet.q4: Only the random session ID (no user data). The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it (also Secure and SameSite=Lax).
sonnet.q5: 12 hours after login (expires_at = login time + 12 hours), because the 30-minute idle limit is never hit and the earlier limit wins.
sonnet.q6: It clears the sid cookie and redirects to /login.
sonnet.q7: It deletes the session named by the sid cookie (if any) before replying, then clears the cookie and redirects to /login. If there is no session, the reply is the same.
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres sessions table. The browser's cookie holds the session ID, and whichever instance receives the request looks that ID up in Postgres (shared by both instances; no sticky sessions).
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table, one row per failed attempt with email and failed_at. How the server decides which failures fall inside the 10-minute window (the exact query) is NOT STATED beyond the rule that 5 failures within any 10-minute period triggers the lock; the cleanup job deletes rows older than 10 minutes.
sonnet.q10: It checks that the session exists, that expires_at is in the future, and that last_seen_at is within the last 30 minutes (one query). When valid, it updates last_seen_at to now.
sonnet.q11: HTTP 503 with the login page message "Sign-in is unavailable right now. Try again shortly." No new cookie is set; the transaction is rolled back and the old session stays.
sonnet.q12: The cleanup job (a timer) deletes sessions past expires_at or idle over 30 minutes. Such sessions already stop working at expiry regardless; the run interval is not chosen yet.
